content_preview.title: Meituan Open-Sources LongCat-2.0, a 1.6-Trillion-Parameter Coding Model It Says Was Trained End-to-End on Chinese Chips
content_preview.summary: Meituan released LongCat-2.0, a 1.6T-parameter MoE model under an MIT license, claiming it is the first trillion-parameter model trained and served entirely on domestic ASICs.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Meituan, the Chinese food-delivery and local-services company, has open-sourced LongCat-2.0, a large language model with 1.6 trillion parameters and a native 1-million-token context window, according to the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3358854/china-debuts-biggest-ai-model-trained-local-chips-meituan-releases-longcat-20). editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (558 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Sections (Overview / What We Know / The Hardware Claim / What We Don't Know) separate reported fact from open questions and consistently foreground that the standout claims are company-supplied.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots read from disk (gzip) and verified against the article. source-0.html.gz (SCMP, status 200): confirms 1.6T parameters, million-token context, release 30 Jun 2026, the verbatim quote 'the industry's first trillion-parameter model to complete full-process training and inference on a 50,000-card domestic computing power cluster', and the DeepSeek V4-pro (launched April) inference-only vs. LongCat full-process distinction. source-1.html.gz (Hugging Face model card, status 200): confirms 1.6T total / ~48B activated, MIT License, >35 trillion training tokens, benchmark scores SWE-bench Pro 59.5 / Terminal-Bench 2.1 70.8 / SWE-bench Multilingual 77.3 / BrowseComp 79.9, GPT-5.5 SWE-bench Pro column 58.6, the three LSA components with verbatim quoted definitions (Streaming-aware, Cross-Layer, Hierarchical Indexing), 'AI ASIC superpods', and Claude Code / OpenClaw / Hermes harness integration. source-2.html.gz (MarkTechPost, status 200): confirms the 33B-56B dynamic activation window, ~48B activated, LSA linear-scaling framing, LongCat-2.0 edging GPT-5.5 (58.6) on SWE-bench Pro, pricing $0.75/$2.95 per million input/output with $0.30/$1.20 launch promotion, and the self-reported caveat ('Every figure below comes from Meituan's own testing', 'Vendor-reported scores', 'Independent leaderboard confirmation is not yet available'). source-3.html.gz (NYU Shanghai RITS, status 200): confirms the 'Owl Alpha' OpenRouter codename, 30 Jun 2026 release, 1.6T MoE, and the pre-training-plus-inference-on-domestic-chips framing. No snapshot failed; no WebFetch fallback needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific, direct quote, and headline/summary/lead claim traces to a cited source. Direct quotes ('the industry's first trillion-parameter model...', the three LSA component definitions, 'Owl Alpha') appear verbatim in their snapshots. The model name (LongCat-2.0) and parameter count (1.6T total / ~48B activated) are confirmed by both the primary Hugging Face card and SCMP. The 'trained end-to-end on Chinese chips' claim is correctly presented as Meituan's own assertion, quoted and attributed to SCMP, and revisited in a dedicated 'The Hardware Claim' section. No hallucinations detected. The internal cross-link to the earlier GLM-5 article resolves to an existing published article.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. The headline's 'It Says' and repeated 'company-reported', 'Meituan says', 'self-reported', and 'if accurate' hedges keep the self-reported hardware and benchmark claims from being stated as independently verified fact. No sensationalism or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior LongCat-2.0 or Meituan-model article in the archive; other Meituan mentions are unrelated (Moonshot funding, platform-pricing rules). Appropriately positioned as an escalation of the GLM-5 'trained on Chinese chips' story rather than a duplicate.
concerns: One source, NYU Shanghai RITS (rits.shanghai.nyu.edu), is not on the source allowlist. It is a university-affiliated tech-summary outlet and every claim it supports (the 'Owl Alpha' OpenRouter codename, the domestic-chips framing) is independently corroborated by the primary SCMP and Hugging Face sources, so it is used only in a corroborating, non-load-bearing role. Judged acceptable editorially; the allowlist was not modified.
recommendations: The pipeline maintainer may consider adding rits.shanghai.nyu.edu to config/source_allowlist.txt if NYU Shanghai RITS is expected to recur as a source.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE. Integrity checks all pass (signature valid, hash valid). All four sources read from snapshot and verified; the model name, 1.6T parameter count, end-to-end-on-Chinese-chips claim, benchmark figures, and all quotes trace to cited sources, with the hardware and benchmark claims properly attributed as company/self-reported and explicitly flagged as not independently verified. The sole finding is an off-allowlist but credible, corroborated source, which is an editorial warning rather than a content defect and does not warrant a public corrections record.
